# Source map — NEWS-010  
**El Universal, “Ingresos del AIFA no bastan ni para pago de la nómina”**

Independent journalism. Financial reporting based on AIFA’s 2022 **“estado de actividades”**, obtained by the outlet, and **“estado analítico de su deuda y otros pasivos.”** No named on-record sources; financial figures are attributed to those documents. Employment and salary figures are attributed to the AIFA Aero website. Author: Noé Cruz Serrano. Published 02-02-23; updated 21-03-23. URL: https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/cartera/mantienen-al-aifa-operando-traves-de-los-subsidios/

## Observed facts

- **F1.** Between 21 March 2022, the inauguration date, and 31 December 2022, the fiscal authorities injected **1.282 billion pesos** into AIFA through subsidies and transfers, **“para evitar cerrar con pérdidas,”** according to its financial statements for year-end 2022. *(block 1, paragraph beginning “Entre el 21 de marzo…”)*
- **F2.** Transfers totaled **564 million pesos by September 2022**, according to prior reporting by *El Universal* published on 3 November 2022. *(block 1, paragraph beginning “La cantidad es más del doble…”)*
- **F3.** The outlet states that the year-end transfer amount was **a little more than 100 times** the support received in 2021, which it estimates at **around 12 million pesos**. *(block 1, paragraph beginning “Al final del ejercicio…”)*
- **F4.** AIFA’s 2022 statement of activities reported **139 million pesos in own-source revenue from the sale of goods and services**, compared with **384 million pesos in payroll costs**. *(block 2, paragraph beginning “El estado de actividades…”)*
- **F5.** Total 2022 **“ingresos y otros beneficios”** were **1.421 billion pesos**: 139 million pesos in own-source revenue from sales of goods and services; 1.282 billion pesos in transfers, allocations, subsidies, and other aid; 205,700 pesos in financial income; and 2,954 pesos in other miscellaneous income and benefits. The article states that **90 centavos of each peso** came from federal-government transfers, allocations, subsidies, and other aid. *(block 2, paragraphs beginning “En total, el AIFA obtuvo…” and “Del total de ingresos…”)*
- **F6.** Of those resources, **829 million pesos (58.3%)** went to general services, for which no breakdown was provided; **384 million pesos (27.0%)** went to personal services, described as employees’ salaries and benefits or payroll; **69 million pesos (4.8%)** went to materials and supplies; and **7.342 million pesos** went to amortization and other expenses. *(block 3, first three paragraphs)*
- **F7.** After reconciling total income with expenses and other losses, AIFA reported savings of **132,686,747.63 pesos**. *(block 3, paragraph beginning “Al conciliar el total…”)*
- **F8.** In 2022, AIFA transported **912,415 passengers** and carried out **8,996 operations**. *(block 1, article standfirst; block 3, paragraph beginning “Con los apoyos otorgados…”)*
- **F9.** By year-end 2022, AIFA had received **876,046 domestic passengers**: Quintana Roo, 241,810; Jalisco, 181,955; Baja California, 127,237; Nuevo León, 101,861; Yucatán, 83,684; Oaxaca, 72,439; Baja California Sur, 30,839; Guerrero, 20,190; Veracruz, 10,811; Tabasco, 4,059; and other destinations, 1,161. *(block 3, paragraph beginning “Al cierre de 2022…”)*
- **F10.** International passenger movements were **17,116 jointly with Cuba and Venezuela**, **11,685 with Panama**, and **582 with other destinations**. *(block 3, paragraph beginning “En cuanto a pasajeros internacionales…”)*
- **F11.** From 1 January to 31 December 2022, AIFA’s total liabilities increased from **30.761 million pesos to 371.757 million pesos**. The article states that they multiplied by 12. The year-end commitments were broken down as **362 million pesos in short-term accounts payable**, **3.7 million pesos in short-term deferred liabilities**, and **5.5 million pesos in third-party funds and assets held in guarantee and/or short-term administration**. *(block 3, paragraph beginning “El AIFA también tuvo…”; block 4, first two paragraphs)*
- **F12.** According to the AIFA Aero website, the terminal had **761 trust employees**. Director Isidoro Pastor Román received **113,954 pesos monthly**; deputy directors, 64,803 pesos; general managers, 41,270 pesos; airport firefighters, 13,755 pesos; and airport executive professionals, 16,161 pesos monthly. *(block 2, paragraphs beginning “El portal web AIFA Aero…” and “Los sueldos más bajos…”)*

## Author assertions and interpretation

- **A1.** “90 centavos de cada peso que la terminal reporta como ingresos fueron ayudas del gobierno.” *(block 1, standfirst)*
- **A2.** The financial statements state that SHCP transfers **“buscan compensar las pérdidas de la nueva terminal, que gasta más de lo que ingresa.”** *(block 2, first paragraph)*
- **A3.** AIFA reported savings of 132,686,747.63 pesos, **“apoyado en una gran cantidad de subsidios.”** *(block 3, paragraph beginning “Al conciliar el total…”)*
- **A4.** “Con los apoyos otorgados a la nueva terminal aérea, el gobierno federal subsidió prácticamente todas sus operaciones en 2022.” *(block 3, paragraph beginning “Con los apoyos otorgados…”)*
- **A5.** “Deuda al alza”; AIFA “tuvo un tropezón en 2022 en materia de pasivos.” *(block 3, final heading and paragraph)*

## Qualifications

- **Q1.** The article states that no breakdown was provided for the **829 million pesos in general services**. *(block 3, first paragraph)*
- **Q2.** The 2022 statement of activities was obtained by *El Universal*; the liabilities figures are attributed to AIFA’s analytical statement of debt and other liabilities. *(block 2, paragraph beginning “El estado de actividades…”; block 3, final paragraph)*
- **Q3.** The extract does not report a comparison with the Cuenta Pública or independently reproduce an SHCP comparison. *(blocks 1–4)*
- **Q4.** The extract contains no quoted response from SHCP or AIFA management. *(blocks 1–4)*
- **Q5.** The extract does not discuss favoritism, political beneficiaries, fraud, or eligibility rules. *(blocks 1–4)*

## Allegations and contrary material

No allegations or contrary material are recorded in the extract. The source is independent journalism relying on AIFA financial documents for the financial figures and on the AIFA Aero website for employment and salary figures.

## Reopen requests

- Breakdown of the 829 million pesos in general services.
- Comparison with the 2022 Cuenta Pública.
- Official SHCP or AIFA response.
- Independent audit or supporting detail concerning the liabilities.
